note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English; the alates were observed from a single queen, whose coloration the original states may be faded. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Shows weak affinities with Anenteotermes: the first marginal tooth of the right mandible tends to be slightly reduced and a rudiment of the mixed segment appears in the gut; Astalotermes and Acholotermes show similar trends, but the mandibular tooth proportions of A. brevior and A. epius differ from those of the present species. In A. apocnetus the alate fontanelle is smaller, the ocelli smaller and farther from the compound eyes, and the postclypeus more inflated, while in the worker the midgut–hindgut junction is short and lies to the right of the Malpighian tubule knot, and the enteric valve seat is distinctly trilobed and ventrally placed in the unopened abdomen. A. hilarus has a longer mandibular apical tooth; A. mansuetus is larger, with a more inflated postclypeus and a large, circular fontanelle, and its worker enteric valve seat is ventral with pronounced trilobation; A. pacatus has large compound eyes and ocelli, and the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible only just clears the molar plate; A. prosenus is very large, with a circular, shallow fontanelle and a longer mandibular apical tooth. The worker abdomen is non-dehiscent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule and pilosity pale yellow, the hairs very sparse and scattered, inconspicuous. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.27, Pcl/Ri 2.02. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.48, Ra/Ri 0.67; a broad, deep notch, in surface view, separates the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible from the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 7.70; the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are roughly aligned, the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth equal, Ra/Ri·Rm 11.96. Fore tibia very slender, Ti/Tw 6.02; third apical spur distinct, half the length of the other two. At the midgut–hindgut junction the midgut overlap is about twice as long as the width of the midgut at the origin of the Malpighian tubules, and the hindgut reaches half of the Malpighian tubule knot; in the unopened abdomen the enteric valve seat is slightly dorsal, with two distinct lateral lobes and a reduced third inner lobe, and is joined to the second hindgut pouch by a conspicuous long neck; the valve membrane bears extremely sparse minute spines outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brown, dark brown above the ocelli, the colour possibly faded. Fontanelle only slightly smaller than the ocellus, elongate-elliptical, slightly raised, yellowish brown; central spot elliptical, about half the fontanelle, slightly raised, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus yellowish brown, labrum yellow; frontal groove very distinct, a slightly concave yellowish brown crescent; antennae yellowish brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum yellowish brown, transverse sutures weak; femora pale yellowish brown, tibiae and tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites yellowish brown with darker dorsal spiracles, ventral spiracles and sternites pale yellowish brown, paler medially; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule not very evenly rounded, slightly undulate; ocelli moderate, their distance from the compound eye three quarters of their minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.25, posterior margin broadly arcuate, median suture distinct. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.53, Ra/Ri 0.70; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is remote from the molar prominence, L4/L1·Lm 6.00; the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are roughly aligned, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth slightly shorter than that of the second. Meso- and metanotum moderately broad at the constriction, M/W 0.30. Cephalic pilosity yellowish brown, the short hairs rather even and almost forming a layer, but obscured by numerous irregular outstanding setae.
